subject: Critical Thinking
title: Anchoring Bias: The First Number Wins
description: A 60-second lesson on Anchoring Bias: The First Number Wins.

hook.text: A store marks a jacket at $500, then 'discounts' it to $250. You feel a bargain. The jacket cost $80 to make.

buildup.text: Anchoring: the first number you see biases every subsequent estimate — even when it's completely irrelevant.

discovery.text: Tversky & Kahneman spun a random wheel, then asked people to estimate African UN countries.

twist.text: Even experts anchor. Real estate agents shown different listing prices valued the same house differently.

climax.text: Anchoring works because System 1 seizes the first number and System 2 adjusts — but always insufficiently.

punchline.text: Whoever sets the first number controls the negotiation.

quiz.question: Why does anchoring bias occur?
options: The first number frames all subsequent judgments, and adjustment is insufficient

details.summary: Anchoring bias causes you to rely too heavily on the first piece of information you encounter. An initial number, even if arbitrary, sets a reference point that drags all subsequent estimates toward it.
details.whyItMatters: Negotiators, marketers, and salespeople exploit anchoring constantly. Recognizing it protects you from being manipulated by strategically chosen first offers.
takeaways: The first number in a negotiation sets the anchor
Even random anchors shift estimates significantly
Counter-anchoring with your own strong first number is the best defense

faq.question: How does anchoring bias affect salary negotiations specifically?
faq.answer: Whoever states the first number sets the anchor. If an employer opens with a low offer, all subsequent negotiation gravitates toward that figure. Starting with your own researched number shifts the anchor in your favor.

faq.question: Can anchoring bias influence decisions even when you know about it?
faq.answer: Yes. Studies show that even participants warned about anchoring still shift their estimates toward the anchor. Awareness helps but does not eliminate the effect. Structured processes are needed as well.
